data.title: Hidden Message
data.solution:
import string

def get_character(time):
    minute = int(time.split(":")[1])
    letter_index = minute % 26

    return string.ascii_uppercase[letter_index]


def increment(char):
    next_letter_index = (string.ascii_uppercase.index(char) + 1) % 26

    return string.ascii_uppercase[next_letter_index]


def find_offset(message):
    offset = 0

    while "FRIEND" not in message:
        message = "".join(list(map(increment, message)))
        offset += 1

    return (message, offset)


n = int(input())
initial_message = []

for i in range(n):
    initial_message.append(get_character(input()))

(final_message, offset) = find_offset(initial_message)

print(offset)
print(final_message)
data.statement:
Your friend lives in a country where the government regularly spies on its citizens. Communication with them is dangerous if they are targeted. In order to circumvent monitoring, you develop a hidden communication system.

Your friend has a social media account where they regularly post innocuous content. When they post, the date and time of the post is displayed underneath it. Using only the time {{HH:MM}}, each post can be translated into a single letter of the English alphabet. A set of posts can be used to communicate a message.

Your friend also decides to use a Caesar cipher (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caesar_cipher) offset for their message. The offset can have a value between 1 and 25 <<inclusive>>, and will be the same across all posts. The resulting message will always contain the word {{FRIEND}}.

A letter is derived from a post with these steps:

1. Take the minute value from the post time (00 - 59)
2. Modulus that number by 26
3. The resulting number becomes the index for the corresponding letter in the English alphabet:

0 -> A, 1 -> B, 2 -> C, ... 23 -> X, 24 -> Y, 25 -> Z

Thus:
09:04 -> E
10:01 -> B
22:08 -> I
23:00 -> A

For example, the minute values [04,01,08,08,11,02,14,05,01,10,00] produce the initial string "EBIILCOFBKA"

After you have produced the initial string, advance all characters in the string forward (wrapping around as necessary) by the same offset until you find the hidden message. In the example above, using an offset of {{3}} produces the message "HELLOFRIEND".

Given a list of social media post dates and times, find the Caesar cipher offset used (0 - 25) and the hidden message they produce.

Goal

1. Take the minute value from the post time (00 - 59)
2. Modulus that number by 26
3. The resulting number becomes the index for the corresponding letter in the English alphabet:

0 -> A, 1 -> B, 2 -> C, ... 23 -> X, 24 -> Y, 25 -> Z

Thus:
09:04 -> E
10:01 -> B
22:08 -> I
23:00 -> A

Given a list of social media post dates and times, find the Caesar cipher offset used (0 - 25) and the hidden message they produce.
Input
Line 1: Integer n for the number of posts
Next n lines: A list of social media post times in the format HH:MM
Output
Line 1: The Caesar cipher offset
Line 2: The hidden message (in uppercase)
Constraints
2 ≤ n ≤ 40
Example
Input
11
20:04
21:01
21:08
21:08
21:11
22:02
22:14
23:05
00:01
00:10
01:00
Output
3
HELLOFRIEND
